items.prompt: Define a business plan. [2]
items.canonical_answer: A business plan is a document containing the business objectives and important details about the operations and finance of the firm. It explains what the enterprise intends to do, for whom, how it will operate and how it expects to finance the activity. It supports coordinated decisions, communication with potential funders and later review. Forecasts are assumptions to test, not promises that sales or funding will occur. A useful plan connects its sections: planned demand must fit capacity, staffing, spending and cash timing. A polished document cannot compensate for unrealistic evidence. Review the plan when conditions change rather than treating completion of the document as completion of the business.
marking_guidance: Meaning: A business plan is a document containing the business objectives and important details about the operations and finance of the firm.

items.prompt: Explain why Omi’s sales, production and financial sections must use compatible assumptions. Fictional Omi Bags predicts many orders but its production plan provides one worker and equipment capable of much less output. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A business plan includes a description of the business, market research, a marketing plan, production plan, organisational plan, financial plan and action plan. The description establishes the proposal and objectives. Research supports demand assumptions; marketing explains the target and offering; production explains how output will be supplied; organisation allocates responsibilities; finance sets out needs, sources and forecasts; the action plan turns decisions into timed tasks. These are connected components, not interchangeable names. Compare assumptions across them: a large sales target is inconsistent with too little capacity unless the plan explains how capacity will change. A production schedule alone leaves ownership, demand and finance unanswered. The sections need reconciliation before commitment. Either establish feasible extra resources or revise the sales expectation; copying the high forecast into every section does not make it realistic.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: A business plan includes a description of the business, market research, a marketing plan, production plan, organisational plan, financial plan and action plan.

items.prompt: Explain why fictional Oru Bags’ equipment list and production schedule are not its entire business plan. [6]

The wider plan also needs the business description, research, marketing, organisation, finance and action arrangements. A technically feasible process alone does not establish customers or cash availability.

items.prompt: Explain how a clear business description helps readers assess Nela’s proposal. Fictional Nela Meals proposes a sole-owned weekday lunch collection service near a workplace cluster in Tsumeb. [6]
items.canonical_answer: This component identifies the proposed activity, ownership arrangement, location, objectives and main offering. It gives readers a clear basis for understanding the remaining sections. State a realistic purpose and scope rather than claiming the enterprise will be successful because it exists. The description is not a substitute for evidence of demand or a cash forecast. Original description: provide one affordable portable lunch range to nearby workers, begin with a limited trial and review repeat paid orders before expanding. The scope makes later capacity and marketing decisions more specific.

items.prompt: Explain how Hela should present its demand evidence and its limitation. Fictional Hela Lunches has neutral interviews with nearby workers but no paid-sales trial. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The research component records the information supporting demand and customer assumptions, including sources, methods, findings and limitations. Show why the information fits the target market and what remains untested. Old regional data or favourable comments alone may not establish local paid demand. The plan should identify the next evidence needed, not hide uncertainty behind a precise-looking sales figure. Its plan can report preferences and the sample limit, then schedule a small trial at the proposed price. It should not label every interested interviewee a confirmed daily customer.

items.prompt: Explain how Nela’s marketing plan should connect target, offering, price and access. Fictional Nela Meals can prepare one weekday range and use local collection. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The marketing plan states target customers, marketing objectives and coordinated choices of product, price, promotion and distribution. It explains how the enterprise will reach and serve its chosen market within a budget. It differs from research, which provides evidence, and from a single advertisement, which is one action. Targets should be reviewable and consistent with operational capacity. Original marketing plan: target nearby workers seeking quick lunch; offer a portable meal at a tested feasible price; use a small accessible notice and direct information to nearby workplaces; provide prearranged collection; limit initial orders to confirmed capacity; review paid orders and repeat purchases weekly. This connects customer need with the whole offer.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: The marketing plan states target customers, marketing objectives and coordinated choices of product, price, promotion and distribution.

items.prompt: Explain why Nela’s production plan needs capacity and input details. Fictional Nela Meals will prepare a limited set of lunches before collection. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The production plan explains how goods or services will be supplied: methods, equipment, inputs, suppliers, premises, capacity, timing and quality arrangements. It translates the sales proposal into a feasible operation. Job, batch and flow production are different methods developed in topic 4.5; the selected method must fit volume and variety. The plan is one part of the whole document, not the entire business plan. Its production component should specify ingredient supply, safe preparation resources, staff tasks, maximum feasible daily meals, collection timing and quality checks. Unconfirmed sales above that capacity need a revised operation, not an unexplained promise.

items.prompt: Explain how Eha should allocate responsibilities in its organisational plan. Fictional Eha Bags has one owner and one assistant. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The organisational plan identifies roles, responsibilities, staffing and reporting. It shows who will carry out the proposed work and which skills are needed. A small business still needs responsibility for buying, production, customer contact and records even when one person performs several roles. Include relevant development needs; training may be on-the-job or off-the-job as explained in topic 3.5. A list of impressive titles does not provide the people or capabilities. The plan can allocate purchasing and finance oversight to the owner and specified preparation work to the assistant, while stating who checks quality and handles customers. Tasks should fit available time rather than assume one person can do everything simultaneously.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: The organisational plan identifies roles, responsibilities, staffing and reporting.

items.prompt: Explain why Ota’s financial plan needs cash timing as well as a profit forecast. Fictional Ota Crafts expects to buy materials before collecting customer payments. [6]
items.canonical_answer: The financial plan identifies start-up and operating needs, finance sources, expected income and costs and cash timing. Explain assumptions and whether funding is agreed or only proposed. Profit forecasts and cash forecasts answer different questions: a credit sale can add profit before receipt. Test whether payments fall due before funds arrive. A lender assesses viability and repayment, so a document full of unsupported optimistic figures is weak evidence. The plan should show the material-payment dates and likely receipts, identify the temporary funding need and state how it would be covered. Calling the future sale profitable does not resolve that timing gap.

items.prompt: Explain how Nela’s action plan can link tasks, responsibility and timing. Fictional Nela Meals plans a limited launch after checking demand and resources. [6]
items.canonical_answer: An action plan turns the proposal into specific tasks, responsible people, deadlines and dependencies. It lets managers coordinate implementation and check progress. A deadline should allow prerequisite work: equipment cannot be tested before it is obtained and staff cannot use a process safely before relevant preparation. Review missed tasks and revise the schedule where necessary rather than record dates without follow-up. Original action extract: owner completes customer-price trial in week 1; owner confirms input supplier and capacity in week 2; team tests preparation and collection in week 3; owner reviews finance before accepting week-4 orders. Each later task depends on the preceding evidence and resources.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: An action plan turns the proposal into specific tasks, responsible people, deadlines and dependencies.

items.prompt: Explain how Tula should use its plan when the trial contradicts its forecast. Fictional Tula Repairs plans a new service but a paid trial produces fewer orders than forecast. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A business plan helps set goals, define the product, identify the consumer, organise research, coordinate marketing and seek finance. It can reveal gaps before money is committed and provide a reference against which actual progress is reviewed. A potential lender can assess the proposal and repayment assumptions, but a plan does not guarantee approval. Managers can assign actions and investigate differences between forecast and actual results. The plan should be updated when evidence changes: a lost customer can affect production, promotion and cash together. Uses are the decisions the document supports; elements are its contents. Explain the link rather than merely repeating a section heading. Use the results to revise demand and resource commitments, then update finance and the action timetable. Ignoring the evidence to preserve the original document would defeat the planning purpose.

items.prompt: Explain how a plan helps Hena set and review a meaningful goal. Fictional Hena Print targets a reliable small-order service and monitors on-time completion over its first month. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A business plan makes objectives explicit and provides a basis for reviewing progress. A defined result and period help distinguish a successful action from merely being busy. Goals must fit resources and should be revised through evidence rather than adjusted just to conceal failure. The plan provides a standard for review. A large number of leaflets distributed would not by itself prove that the service goal was met.

items.prompt: Explain how planning can help Tano choose a feasible product range. Fictional Tano Bags considers many styles but can reliably produce one durable range. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A plan helps define the product or service and test whether its features meet customer needs within capacity and cost limits. It can reveal that an attractive feature is unaffordable or impractical. The product should fit the wider offer: promised variety affects equipment, inputs and staffing as well as promotion. Planning exposes the mismatch and supports a focused feasible launch rather than an unsupported promise of variety.

items.prompt: Explain how a defined consumer helps Nalu coordinate its offer. Fictional Nalu Meals targets nearby workers with short breaks. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A plan identifies who is expected to buy, the need served and how those consumers can be reached. This helps prevent production for an undefined everyone. Consumer interest must include the ability and willingness to pay the feasible price, not merely liking the idea. A narrow target also creates dependence that should be recognised. Its plan can align portability and collection speed with that need. Tourist evening menus would be a different consumer offer requiring separate evidence and capability.

items.prompt: Explain how Omi’s plan should guide the next research priority. Fictional Omi Furniture knows workshop capacity but not whether buyers will pay its proposed price. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Planning helps identify missing information, choose relevant research and decide what evidence should precede investment. It can prioritise an unknown price response over collecting facts already available. Research has a cost, so link it to a consequential uncertainty rather than gather unrelated statistics. Findings should update the plan when they contradict initial assumptions. The next study should test price and demand among suitable buyers. Another description of machinery would not close that market gap.

items.prompt: Explain why a lender needs a coherent plan rather than Tula’s sales goal alone. Fictional Tula Tools seeks a loan for equipment and presents cost, customer evidence and repayment forecasts. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A plan communicates the proposal, funding need, expected return and cash assumptions to potential finance providers. It can help lenders or investors assess risk, while helping owners see whether finance is affordable. It does not create an entitlement to a loan or guarantee that forecasts will occur. State the requested amount and use, supporting evidence and contingencies clearly. The lender can assess whether expected cash supports instalments. A high sales goal without cost or receipt evidence would be less persuasive and does not establish repayment capacity.

items.prompt:
Fictional Hela Meals has checked equipment capacity and preparation costs for a small service. Its draft plan includes marketing, production, organisation, finance and an action timetable, but sales rely on the owner’s guess rather than customer evidence. The owner has time for one further investigation before deciding whether to commit.

a(i) Define a business plan. [2]
a(ii) State two uses of a business plan. [2]
b State two operational details a business plan should explain. [2]
c Explain why Hela’s market and financial sections must be connected. [6]
d Evaluate whether investigating demand or repeating the equipment check should be the next priority. [8]
items.canonical_answer: a(i) A document containing business objectives and important details of operations and finance. a(ii) Reviewing goals and communicating a finance proposal. b Required equipment and staffing responsibilities. c Sales assumptions determine expected income and production volume, which affect input spending and cash needs. Unsupported demand can therefore make an apparently precise financial forecast unreliable. Research findings should update both marketing and finance, not sit as an unrelated appendix. d Demand is the critical untested assumption, while capacity is already checked. Prioritise suitable customer and price evidence, recognising that research costs time and still cannot guarantee sales. Retain the equipment and other sections; prioritising one investigation does not justify omitting required components.

Fictional Ota Bags has a coherent draft plan and verified workshop capacity and costs. Demand at its proposed price remains untested. The owner compares further market investigation with repeating the completed capacity check.

items.prompt:
Fictional Ota Bags has a coherent draft plan and verified workshop capacity and costs. Demand at its proposed price remains untested. The owner compares further market investigation with repeating the completed capacity check. For part (b) only, a dependable paid-order agreement now verifies sufficient demand at the proposed price, while the intended machine becomes unavailable and replacement capacity is unknown. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate demand research against another capacity check at Ota under the original facts. [12]
b Evaluate the priority after the order agreement and machine change. Explain whether the judgement changes. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a Demand is the missing evidence with consequences across the forecast, so prioritise suitable customer and price research. Repeating verified capacity work is less useful unless new facts question it. The plan should schedule the research and update all affected assumptions. b Demand now has dependable paid-order support, but unavailable machinery makes capacity uncertain. Prioritise the production alternative and its cost, timing and financing before promising delivery. The recommendation changes because the unresolved constraint changes. Update the action and financial plans too; do not discard marketing or assume the new machine will be affordable simply because orders exist.
